extracted.intended_audience: readers, sources, donors, potential sponsors, community members, and journalists interested in Chalkbeat's mission and standards
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational editorial values and operational standards for a nonprofit local education newsroom, describing what Chalkbeat aims to produce, how it protects independence, and how it measures impact. Useful for assessing or emulating Chalkbeat-style local education reporting and newsroom practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: One essential story
rubrics_metrics.description: We believe that all children deserve access to a quality education — one that prepares them for the duties of citizenship in a democracy and connects them to economic opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chalkbeat is passionate about cultivating the expertise and constant curiosity necessary to tell the vital and nuanced story of education in America with authority. Emphasizes focusing coverage on the core, substantive issues affecting students' access to quality education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy, fairness, and independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Our mission demands that our readers and sources alike be able to have the utmost confidence in the accuracy of our journalism; the fairness of our reporting process; and the independence of our news judgments from the influence of advocates and financial supporters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are core commitments that guide reporting choices and processes; they imply rigorous fact-checking, fair treatment of subjects, and procedures to avoid undue influence from funders or advocates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power in independence (no predetermined advocacy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our unique impact as journalists lies in our ability to tell the full and complete story, without consideration of profit, ideology, or advocacy. We take no predetermined position on how to achieve better schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work to build a business model and newsroom practices that safeguard editorial independence. Journalists should avoid advocacy positions and report comprehensively so readers can form their own judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Going local (deep community-rooted coverage)
rubrics_metrics.description: We don’t do flyovers and never parachute in. We put down roots in the communities we cover and work with our readers as well as for them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover local people, institutions, and systems with depth and continuity — treating local education actors with the same importance as higher-profile subjects; engage with readers and sources in the community rather than transient or superficial coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact-oriented reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing stories is not enough. We are on a mission to get the full truth to the maximum people at the moments of greatest consequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting should be shaped to bring stories, people, and stakes alive so readers can engage in informed action and debate. Emphasizes distribution, timing, and storytelling techniques that increase practical civic impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antiracism
rubrics_metrics.description: We acknowledge and condemn the ongoing legacy of racism in U.S. public education and in the institution we are part of, the press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commit to standing against racism in organizational building and daily reporting. This implies attention to racial equity in story selection, framing, sourcing, and institutional practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness and diversity in coverage and staff
rubrics_metrics.description: We write about people who have historically lacked access to a quality education. In doing so, we hope to amplify their voices and help empower them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for team composition and reporting practices that represent and are truly open to the communities covered; prioritize including historically marginalized voices and perspectives in reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investing in staff development
rubrics_metrics.description: We strive to connect every member of our team with the opportunities and challenges they need to learn and grow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate resources and organizational practices for professional development, mentorship, and growth so staff can meet ambitious reporting goals; invest in the newsroom as a means to sustain quality coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversified revenue to protect editorial independence
rubrics_metrics.description: One way we protect our commitment to accuracy, integrity, and independence is by actively designing a business model that relies on diversified streams of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revenue sources include major foundation and individual donations, reader contributions, paid sponsorships on site and newsletters, sponsored live events, and a paid jobs board. The guidance is to diversify funding so no single source can unduly influence editorial judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent sponsorship practices (sponsors as support, not editorial influence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chalkbeat’s support comes from a diverse mix of sources, including sponsors who pay for opportunities to share messages with our readers and donors who believe in our mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsorships appear on the website and email newsletters; the organization emphasizes designing sponsorship and business practices so that financial supporters do not shape news judgments. (Page links to supporters and becoming a sponsor for more detail.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of ethics
rubrics_metrics.description: We have adopted a code of ethics to govern the conduct of our team members and those we work with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A formal ethics code provides behavioral and procedural standards for reporters and staff; it is meant to operationalize commitments to accuracy, fairness, and independence. (The page links to the full code for specifics.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure and track reporting impact (MORI)
rubrics_metrics.description: MORI — Measures of Our Reporting’s Influence — a platform for tracking impact; documenting how, why, when, and where we made a difference so we can repeat our success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chalkbeat developed a WordPress plugin (MORI) to track impact and released it open source. Guidance: systematically track impact indicators to learn from outcomes and improve reporting strategies; encourages other newsrooms/devs to use and contribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community accountability via reader advisory board
rubrics_metrics.description: A dynamic and diverse reader advisory board guides our coverage, holds us accountable for meeting our goals, and helps us build strong relationships in the communities we cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use advisory boards with diverse community representation to inform editorial priorities and hold the newsroom accountable. The page lists current members and provides application/contact links for participation.
